description: Dispute-level cases for TechKart triage. Each records one open item-not-received dispute's shipment facts, the response taken, and whether that response was appropriate or backfired. All authored by the MediateAI team from common merchant-operations practice; none is a real incident. Outcomes are qualitative; no case carries a measured win rate.

fingerprint_fields.deadline_first: in transit only: 1 if the response deadline falls before the expected delivery
fingerprint_fields.days_to_due: days left to respond when the response was taken

cases.title: Delivered with a confirmation scan, evidence filed
cases.narrative: Carrier showed a delivered scan at the buyer's address. The merchant filed proof of fulfilment with the carrier, tracking number and the delivery confirmation.
cases.outcome: Dispute closed in the merchant's favour. Illustrative, no measured numbers.

cases.title: High-value parcel delivered with confirmation
cases.narrative: A watch order showed a delivered scan. The merchant filed the delivery confirmation and order record before the deadline.

cases.title: Delivered with GPS location and photo
cases.narrative: The carrier's record included the GPS location of the drop-off. The merchant attached the GPS record alongside the delivery confirmation.

cases.title: Delivered against a recipient signature
cases.narrative: The parcel was signed for. The merchant included the signature record with the proof of fulfilment.

cases.title: Delivered, but only a tracking number was sent
cases.narrative: Delivery had been confirmed, but the merchant only pasted the tracking number and no delivery status.
cases.outcome: Backfired: a tracking number alone did not show delivery and the dispute was lost. Include the delivery confirmation itself.

cases.title: In transit, arriving well before the deadline
cases.narrative: The parcel was delayed at a carrier hub but scanned moving, with delivery expected in three days. The merchant messaged the buyer with the tracking link and real delivery window, and re-checked before the deadline.
cases.outcome: Parcel arrived; the buyer closed the dispute. Illustrative.

cases.title: In transit, buyer reassured with the delivery window
cases.narrative: A battery order was still moving. The merchant explained the delay and gave the carrier's estimate.
cases.outcome: Buyer withdrew the dispute after delivery. Illustrative.

cases.title: In transit, but the deadline came first
cases.narrative: The parcel would not arrive before the response deadline. The merchant responded in time with the tracking record, the ship date and the delivery window stated at checkout, saying plainly that it was still in transit.
cases.outcome: The dispute stayed open until delivery and was then resolved. Illustrative.

cases.title: Late parcel answered truthfully before the deadline
cases.narrative: A delayed watch order had no chance of arriving before the deadline. The merchant submitted shipment proof and the agreed window instead of waiting.

cases.title: In transit, but the merchant claimed it was delivered
cases.narrative: To beat the deadline, the merchant submitted the tracking number as proof of delivery while the parcel was still moving.
cases.outcome: Backfired: the tracking page contradicted the claim, the dispute was lost and the buyer complained. Never claim delivery that has not happened.

cases.title: In transit, merchant waited for delivery and missed the deadline
cases.narrative: The merchant held off responding until the parcel arrived. The deadline passed first.
cases.outcome: Backfired: the dispute closed in the buyer's favour by default. Waiting only works when the window allows it.

cases.title: Carrier confirmed the parcel lost
cases.narrative: The carrier confirmed the parcel lost in its network. The merchant refunded the buyer and filed a claim with the carrier for the parcel's value.
cases.outcome: Buyer kept; carrier claim recovered part of the cost. Illustrative.

cases.title: High-value parcel lost in a carrier hub
cases.narrative: A watch went missing after a hub scan. The merchant accepted the claim and pursued the carrier.
cases.outcome: Resolved with the buyer; carrier claim filed. Illustrative.

cases.title: Lost parcel contested with its tracking number
cases.narrative: The merchant submitted the tracking number of a parcel the carrier had already declared lost.
cases.outcome: Backfired: the evidence showed the loss, the dispute was lost anyway and the buyer escalated. Do not contest a parcel you know is lost.

cases.title: No tracking on file: records gathered first
cases.narrative: No tracking number had been uploaded. The merchant pulled the warehouse dispatch log and asked the carrier for a trace before deciding how to respond.
cases.outcome: The trace showed the parcel had been delivered; the merchant then responded with evidence. Illustrative.

cases.title: No tracking on file: responded without checking
cases.narrative: With no tracking to hand, the merchant refunded straight away without checking dispatch records.
cases.outcome: Backfired: the parcel had been delivered, so the refund was money lost. Check the records before acting.
